verses.1: Tax collectors and sinners were all coming near to him to hear him.
verses.2: The Pharisees and scribes grumbled, saying, "This man receives sinners and eats with them."
verses.3: He told them this parable, saying:
verses.4: "What man among you, having a hundred sheep and losing one of them, does not leave the ninety-nine in the wilderness and go after the lost one until he finds it?
verses.5: And upon finding it, he places it on his shoulders, rejoicing.
verses.6: Then, returning home, he calls together his friends and neighbors, saying to them, 'Rejoice with me, for I have found my lost sheep.'
verses.7: I say to you that in heaven there is greater joy over one sinner who repents than over ninety-nine righteous people who have no need to repent.
verses.8: "Or what woman, having ten silver coins and losing one of them, would not light a lamp and sweep the house and search carefully until she finds it?
verses.9: And upon finding it, she calls together her friends and neighbors, saying, 'Rejoice with me, for I have found the silver coin I lost.'
verses.10: In the same way, I tell you, there is joy among the angels of God over one sinner who repents."
verses.11: He continued, "A man had two sons.
verses.12: And the younger of them said to his father, 'Father, give me the share of the property that belongs to me.' So he divided his living with them.
verses.13: Not many days later, the younger son gathered everything and went to a distant country, and there he squandered his property by living wastefully.
verses.14: After he had spent everything, a severe famine arose in that country, and he began to be in need.
verses.15: So he went and joined himself to a citizen of that country, and he sent him to his fields to feed pigs.
verses.16: He longed to be filled with the pods that the pigs were eating, but no one gave anything to him.
verses.17: But coming to himself, he said, 'How many of my father’s hired men have more than enough food, while I am perishing with hunger here!
verses.18: I will get up and go to my father and say to him, "Father, I have sinned toward heaven and before you.
verses.19: I am no longer worthy to be called your son. Make me like one of your hired men."'
verses.20: So he got up and went to his father. But while he was still far off, his father saw him and was filled with compassion, and ran and fell on his neck and kissed him.
verses.21: But the son said to him, 'Father, I have sinned toward heaven and before you. I am no longer worthy to be called your son.'
verses.22: But the father said to his slaves, 'Quick, bring out the best robe and put it on him, and put a ring on his hand and sandals on his feet,
verses.23: and bring the fattened calf, slaughter it, and let us eat and celebrate,
verses.24: for this son of mine was dead and has come back to life; he was lost and has been found.' And they began to celebrate.
verses.25: Now his older son was in the field. And as he came and drew near to the house, he heard music and dancing.
verses.26: He called one of the servants and asked what these things could be.
verses.27: The servant said to him, 'Your brother has come, and your father has slaughtered the fattened calf because he has received him back in good health.'
verses.28: But he became angry and refused to go in. So his father came out and pleaded with him.
verses.29: But he answered his father, 'Look, these many years I have been serving you and never disobeyed your command. And yet you never gave me even a young goat so that I could celebrate with my friends.
verses.30: But when this son of yours who devoured your living with prostitutes came, you slaughtered the fattened calf for him!'
verses.31: But the father said to him, 'Son, you are always with me, and everything I have is yours.
verses.32: But we had to celebrate and be glad, for this brother of yours was dead and has come to life, he was lost and has been found.'"

notes:
Notes
- v. 10: "among the angels of God" — the phrase "ἐνώπιον τῶν ἀγγέλων τοῦ θεοῦ" is rendered as "among the angels of God" to reflect the spatial context of celebration in heaven.
- v. 16: "pods that the pigs were eating" — "κερατίων" is translated as "pods" based on the context of pig feed in ancient agrarian settings.
- v. 20: "coming to himself" — "ἐις ἑαυτὸν ἐλθὼν" is rendered as "coming to himself" to capture the internal realization in the narrative.
raw:
[1] Tax collectors and sinners were all coming near to him to hear him.

[2] The Pharisees and scribes grumbled, saying, "This man receives sinners and eats with them."

[3] He told them this parable, saying:

[4] "What man among you, having a hundred sheep and losing one of them, does not leave the ninety-nine in the wilderness and go after the lost one until he finds it?

[5] And upon finding it, he places it on his shoulders, rejoicing.

[6] Then, returning home, he calls together his friends and neighbors, saying to them, 'Rejoice with me, for I have found my lost sheep.'

[7] I say to you that in heaven there is greater joy over one sinner who repents than over ninety-nine righteous people who have no need to repent.

[8] "Or what woman, having ten silver coins and losing one of them, would not light a lamp and sweep the house and search carefully until she finds it?

[9] And upon finding it, she calls together her friends and neighbors, saying, 'Rejoice with me, for I have found the silver coin I lost.'

[10] In the same way, I tell you, there is joy among the angels of God over one sinner who repents."

[11] He continued, "A man had two sons.

[12] And the younger of them said to his father, 'Father, give me the share of the property that belongs to me.' So he divided his living with them.

[13] Not many days later, the younger son gathered everything and went to a distant country, and there he squandered his property by living wastefully.

[14] After he had spent everything, a severe famine arose in that country, and he began to be in need.

[15] So he went and joined himself to a citizen of that country, and he sent him to his fields to feed pigs.

[16] He longed to be filled with the pods that the pigs were eating, but no one gave anything to him.

[17] But coming to himself, he said, 'How many of my father’s hired men have more than enough food, while I am perishing with hunger here!

[18] I will get up and go to my father and say to him, "Father, I have sinned toward heaven and before you.

[19] I am no longer worthy to be called your son. Make me like one of your hired men."'

[20] So he got up and went to his father. But while he was still far off, his father saw him and was filled with compassion, and ran and fell on his neck and kissed him.

[21] But the son said to him, 'Father, I have sinned toward heaven and before you. I am no longer worthy to be called your son.'

[22] But the father said to his slaves, 'Quick, bring out the best robe and put it on him, and put a ring on his hand and sandals on his feet,

[23] and bring the fattened calf, slaughter it, and let us eat and celebrate,

[24] for this son of mine was dead and has come back to life; he was lost and has been found.' And they began to celebrate.

[25] Now his older son was in the field. And as he came and drew near to the house, he heard music and dancing.

[26] He called one of the servants and asked what these things could be.

[27] The servant said to him, 'Your brother has come, and your father has slaughtered the fattened calf because he has received him back in good health.'

[28] But he became angry and refused to go in. So his father came out and pleaded with him.

[29] But he answered his father, 'Look, these many years I have been serving you and never disobeyed your command. And yet you never gave me even a young goat so that I could celebrate with my friends.

[30] But when this son of yours who devoured your living with prostitutes came, you slaughtered the fattened calf for him!'

[31] But the father said to him, 'Son, you are always with me, and everything I have is yours.

[32] But we had to celebrate and be glad, for this brother of yours was dead and has come to life, he was lost and has been found.'"

- v. 10: "among the angels of God" — the phrase "ἐνώπιον τῶν ἀγγέλων τοῦ θεοῦ" is rendered as "among the angels of God" to reflect the spatial context of celebration in heaven.
- v. 16: "pods that the pigs were eating" — "κερατίων" is translated as "pods" based on the context of pig feed in ancient agrarian settings.
- v. 20: "coming to himself" — "ἐις ἑαυτὸν ἐλθὼν" is rendered as "coming to himself" to capture the internal realization in the narrative.
